source.title: Through the LENS: Local Geometric Decomposition of Vision-Language Model Representations
source.authors: Shalom Kachko; Raz Lapid; Margarita Vald; Almog Dubin; Moshe Sipper

record.tranche_reason: The study investigates local geometric neighborhoods in vision-language model activations, not neuron poles or the neuron-based claims in V1–V7. Its reported results concern a related but different interpretability unit.
record.gate_note: The study reports measurements and interventions on MFA neighborhoods, not on individual neurons, neuron poles, neuron explanations, or attribution graphs. The rows below record adjacent findings about local neighborhoods; none tests a listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study decomposes VLM residual-stream activations into MFA Gaussian neighborhoods and evaluates their labeling, steering and retrieval. It never audits individual neurons or neuron poles, never scores neuron explanations by simulation, and builds no neuron-based attribution graphs. Polysemanticity and Bills et al. are mentioned only as background. Its results concern a different interpretability unit (local neighborhoods), so none of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that local low-rank MFA neighborhoods are interpretable and steerable units for cross-modal VLM analysis. They also note limits: only two models, model-based labels and judges, only 80 human-rated outputs, brittle late-layer steering, and no circuit identification.
record.recipe_differences: The paper decomposes VLM residual-stream activations into MFA neighborhoods and evaluates centroid steering and cross-modal retrieval; it does not audit neuron poles or test explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured mixed-neighborhood share changes with modality-purity threshold, component count, and layer; steering performance varies by model, layer, intervention scope, and target modality, and late-layer steering is reported as less reliable.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed MFA-neighborhood shares vary by model and depth. LLaVA goes from 0 to 55 to 472 (0% to 5.7%) across layers 8, 16 and 29. Qwen3-VL goes from 464 to 61 to 128 across layers 9, 18 and 27. Absolute shares scale with the purity threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these two VLMs, the prevalence of modality-mixed local neighborhoods depends on architecture and depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Interpolating activations toward MFA centroids redirected generation within and across modalities at early and middle layers (e.g., Vis→Text 1.244 and Text→Vis 0.921 at LLaVA layer 8). Late-layer steering was brittle, and vision-only scope largely failed there.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local neighborhood centroids act as causal steering targets in VLMs at early and middle layers, but less reliably late.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to two open VLMs and selected datasets and layers. Automated labels and steering scores use model-based judges; human evaluation covers 80 outputs. The authors state that late-layer steering is less reliable and that the method does not identify the circuits producing the neighborhoods.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or their job shares.
No neuron-pole job shares across language models, dense or MoE architectures, or scale.
No study of InceptionV1 cat/car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
No interpretable-neuron shares under different tools or architectures.
No neuron-based attribution graphs or reconstruction-error comparison.
No held-out prediction test of explanations derived from activating examples.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Do not count the mixed-component shares (e.g., 5.7%) as evidence on V1 or V2. They count geometric neighborhoods containing both modalities, not neurons with two jobs. The labeling pipeline resembles the activating-example explanation approach relevant to V6, but the study never tests whether its labels predict activations.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or their main-job shares.
Does not measure neuron-pole job shares across language models, dense and MoE architectures, or model scales up to trillions of parameters.
Does not study InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose detection, or recursive generalization versus superposition.
Does not measure interpretable-neuron shares, InceptionV1-sized vision models, or the stated estimates under different tools or architectures.
Does not evaluate attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons or their reconstruction error.
Does not test whether neuron explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict firing on new activations.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
